text: At midnight, millions of people dropped everything for one video game they waited thirteen years to play.
Grand Theft Auto 6 is finally out. The last one came out in 2013, and it sold over two hundred million copies.
When the first trailer dropped, it got ninety million views in one day, breaking a YouTube record.
Then the game got pushed back. Not once, but twice.
On launch night, fans found a trick. Switch your console to New Zealand, where midnight comes first, and play hours early.
The game is so huge, over two hundred gigabytes, that one internet company broke its download record twice.
Over seventeen million copies sold right away, and almost six million people watched others play it live at the same time.
Reviewers gave it a ninety nine out of a hundred, tying the highest scoring game ever.
But the wildest part came from the Army. One unit offered soldiers four days off to play it.
The catch? They had to sign up for at least two more years in the Army. And some of them actually did it.
Follow for more of the wildest stuff happening right now.
